speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have blisters on your forearm and ulcers on your mucosal surfaces. To understand the cause, are you currently experiencing a fever, sore throat, or a headache? Also, have you noticed a rash on your palms or the soles of your feet?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old female. The patient reports the appearance of blisters on her forearm 3 days ago, accompanied by pain in her left cheek when eating and pain during sexual intercourse for the past week. She has been hiking in the woods recently but denies contact with poison ivy. She has a history of hypertension and osteoarthritis, recently started taking captopril, and discontinued meloxicam 2 weeks ago. Family history includes pernicious anemia and Graves' disease.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Hand-Foot-and-Mouth Disease (HFMD) is unlikely given the patient's age and specific symptoms; the combination of painful oral ulcers (pain when eating), blisters on the forearm, and dyspareunia (pain during intercourse) in a 50-year-old female strongly suggests a diagnosis of Pemphigus Vulgaris or potentially Stevens-Johnson Syndrome (SJS)/Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis (TEN), possibly triggered by recent medication changes or underlying autoimmune conditions. The pain during sexual intercourse is a key differentiator that points towards extensive mucosal involvement typical of Pemphigus Vulgaris. I will request images to assess the extent of skin involvement and blistering. REQUEST IMAGES: Skin_Blisters_and_Mucosal_Ulcers.
